prompt: Implement the broadcasting side of the listener pattern: add/remove listeners, fire only on a real price change, and survive a listener that unsubscribes itself from inside the callback.
explanation: Swing components are just classes that keep a list of listeners and walk it when something happens -- this is that machinery, written out. Firing only when the value really changes is the same rule PropertyChangeSupport follows, and it keeps observers from reacting to writes that changed nothing. Iterating over a fresh copy of the list is what makes re-entrant unsubscribing safe: the copy is untouched while the real list shrinks.
hints: getPrice does double duty -- setPrice can call it to find the old value, including the 0 default for an unknown symbol.
Return early from setPrice when the old and new prices are equal, before touching the map.
new ArrayList<>(listeners) inside the for-each header gives you a snapshot to walk, so removals during the loop cannot break it.
